title: Disciplinary Code and Probation Policy
summary: The disciplinary framework at Pelagos: categories of misconduct, progressive discipline, hearings, appeals and the probation policy.
body:
## 1. PURPOSE

This policy sets out a fair, consistent and firm disciplinary framework for employee conduct and performance at Pelagos. It supports:

- efficient operations in a restaurant environment;
- compliance with South African labour law; and
- enforcement of standards for hygiene, safety, attendance and behaviour.

## 2. APPLICATION

This policy applies to all employees and forms part of their conditions of employment. All employees must comply with it in terms of their employment contract.

## 3. LEGAL FRAMEWORK

This policy is aligned with:

- the Labour Relations Act 66 of 1995 (LRA);
- the Basic Conditions of Employment Act 75 of 1997 (BCEA); and
- the Code of Good Practice: Dismissal (Schedule 8 to the LRA).

## 4. GENERAL PRINCIPLES

- Discipline is corrective, but it will be applied firmly.
- Employees have the right to be heard before disciplinary action is taken.
- The company may move to a higher step depending on how serious the offence is.
- Serious offences may lead to dismissal for a first offence.
- Discipline will be applied consistently to all employees.

## 5. CATEGORIES OF MISCONDUCT

| **5.1 Minor misconduct** | **5.2 Serious misconduct** | **5.3 Gross misconduct** |
|---|---|---|
| Late coming ¶ Poor timekeeping ¶ Minor procedural breaches ¶ Failure to follow instructions ¶ Unauthorised cellphone use ¶ Uniform non-compliance | Repeated minor offences ¶ Insubordination ¶ Absenteeism without notice ¶ Negligence affecting operations ¶ Breach of hygiene or safety rules ¶ Breach of confidentiality | Theft (including food, stock and cash) ¶ Fraud or dishonesty ¶ Assault or threats ¶ Gross insubordination ¶ Serious food safety breach ¶ Sexual harassment ¶ Clocking fraud |

Gross misconduct may result in dismissal without notice (summary dismissal) after a disciplinary hearing, in line with the employment contract.

## 6. PROGRESSIVE DISCIPLINE

| **Step** | **Action**                           | **Valid for**  |
|----------|--------------------------------------|----------------|
| 1        | Verbal warning (recorded in writing) | 3 months       |
| 2        | Written warning                      | 6 months       |
| 3        | Final written warning                | 12 months      |
| 4        | Disciplinary hearing                 | Not applicable |

### Rules

- A repeat offence while a warning is still valid moves straight to the next step.
- Management may skip steps depending on how serious the offence is.
- All warnings must be documented and signed.

## 7. ABSENTEEISM AND ABSCONDMENT

- **Absenteeism without notice:** failing to report for duty without telling management, where the employee intends to return.
- **Abscondment (desertion):** unauthorised absence where there are signs that the employee does not intend to return.

In both cases the company will try to contact the employee, ask for an explanation and, if necessary, hold a disciplinary hearing.

## 8. DISCIPLINARY HEARING PROCEDURE

### 8.1 Notice

The employee will receive written notice of the hearing, including:

- the charges;
- the date, time and venue; and
- their rights at the hearing.

The employee will be given reasonable time to prepare, normally at least 48 hours’ notice.

### 8.2 Rights

At the hearing, the employee may:

- be represented by a fellow employee (or a shop steward, if a trade union is recognised);
- use an interpreter if needed;
- present evidence;
- call witnesses; and
- question the company’s witnesses.

### 8.3 Possible outcomes

- No action.
- Verbal, written or final written warning.
- Dismissal, with or without notice depending on the seriousness of the offence.

## 9. SUSPENSION

An employee may be suspended on full pay as a precaution while an investigation or hearing is pending.

## 10. APPEALS

An appeal must be submitted in writing within **3 working days** of the outcome. Where possible, the appeal will be heard by a manager who was not involved in the original hearing.

## 11. DISCIPLINARY CODE TABLE

| **Offence**                              | **1st offence**  | **2nd offence** | **3rd offence** |
|------------------------------------------|------------------|-----------------|-----------------|
| **Late coming**                          | Verbal           | Written         | Final           |
| **Poor timekeeping**                     | Verbal           | Written         | Final           |
| **Failure to follow instructions**       | Verbal           | Written         | Final           |
| **Unauthorised cellphone use on duty**   | Verbal           | Written         | Final           |
| **Uniform or appearance non-compliance** | Verbal           | Written         | Final           |
| **Absenteeism without notice**           | Written          | Final           | Hearing         |
| **Abscondment**                          | Hearing          | Not applicable  | Not applicable  |
| **Negligence**                           | Written          | Final           | Hearing         |
| **Insubordination**                      | Written          | Final           | Hearing         |
| **Hygiene breach**                       | Written          | Final           | Hearing         |
| **Unsafe practices**                     | Written          | Final           | Hearing         |
| **Breach of confidentiality**            | Written          | Final           | Hearing         |
| **Under the influence at work**          | Final or hearing | Dismissal       | Not applicable  |
| **Verbal abuse**                         | Final            | Hearing         | Dismissal       |
| **Fighting or assault**                  | Hearing          | Dismissal       | Not applicable  |
| **Theft or fraud**                       | Hearing          | Dismissal       | Not applicable  |
| **Clocking fraud**                       | Hearing          | Dismissal       | Not applicable  |
| **Dishonesty**                           | Hearing          | Dismissal       | Not applicable  |
| **Sexual harassment**                    | Hearing          | Dismissal       | Not applicable  |

This table is a guideline. Management may deviate from it depending on how serious the offence is. Dismissal is always decided at a disciplinary hearing.

## 12. PROBATION POLICY

### 12.1 Duration

The first 3 months of employment are a probation period, unless the employment contract says otherwise.

### 12.2 Purpose

Probation is used to assess the employee’s performance, conduct and suitability for the role.

### 12.3 Standards during probation

Employees on probation must:

- meet the performance standards;
- follow all rules and procedures;
- maintain good attendance and punctuality; and
- comply with hygiene and safety standards.

### 12.4 Monitoring

- Regular feedback will be given.
- Performance may be reviewed at any time.

### 12.5 Poor performance or misconduct

If an employee does not meet the required standards or commits misconduct, the company may give guidance or training, issue warnings, or end the employment after a fair process.

### 12.6 Termination during probation

- An employee may be dismissed during probation for poor performance, misconduct or unsuitability.
- A fair procedure will still be followed, although it may be less formal than for permanent employees.

### 12.7 Confirmation of employment

When probation has been completed successfully, the manager confirms this in writing and employment continues on a permanent basis.

## 13. RELATED DOCUMENTS

- PEL-POL-001 Staff Handbook (section 13, Discipline, grievances and performance, and the rules on clocking 4.4, confidentiality 5.2, cellphones 6.3 and uniform 7.2)
- PEL-SOP-011 Staff Onboarding (section 4, Probation management)
